python-in-excel.title: Python in Excel availability – Microsoft Support
python-in-excel.notes: Python in Excel lets users write Python formulas directly in the Excel grid. It is aimed at advanced visualizations and more demanding data analysis, and it gives access to open-source Python libraries under enterprise-level security. Workbooks that use it can be shared and refreshed with colleagues. A paid Microsoft 365 license for the desktop apps is required, and free or perpetual home licenses do not support it; the Microsoft 365 connected experiences must also be switched on. On Windows the feature depends on specific update channels and build versions, and Excel for the web is available to enterprise and business users. Without the add-on license, only standard compute and automatic recalculation are offered, while the add-on adds premium compute plus manual and partial recalculation modes. Premium compute is capped per month and falls back to standard afterwards. Excel for iPad, iPhone and Android cannot recalculate Python cells and shows an error, and device-based subscriptions and shared computer activation are not supported.

account-reconciliation-agent.title: Configure the account reconciliation agent – Microsoft Learn
account-reconciliation-agent.notes: This page explains how a system administrator sets up the account reconciliation agent in Dynamics 365 Finance. The feature is marked as a production-ready preview, so its content and behavior may change. The agent is a Copilot Studio agent that is published automatically unless data loss prevention policies block it. It relies on four Power Automate flows covering work discovery, agent execution, logging of recommended actions and completion of the agent request, plus Dataverse and Copilot Studio connectors. Prerequisites include a minimum Finance version, the Immersive Home, Agent management and Account reconciliation agent features in feature management, and specific Copilot packages installed through the Power Platform admin center. A dedicated agent user with defined roles in both Dataverse and Finance is recommended, and the System agent role is exempt from the usual user license requirements. Deployment can go through a wizard in Copilot Hub or manually with connections and a PowerShell script that activates the flows. The page does not describe reconciliation scenarios or accuracy, and Microsoft may swap the underlying AI model automatically.

active-directory-certificate-services.title: Active Directory Certificate Services overview – Microsoft Learn
active-directory-certificate-services.notes: Active Directory Certificate Services is a Windows Server role for issuing and managing public key infrastructure certificates. Such certificates support encryption, digital signatures and authentication of computers, users and devices. The role binds an identity to a private key and handles enrollment and revocation. Its components include root and subordinate certification authorities, web enrollment, an online responder for revocation status, the Network Device Enrollment Service for devices without domain accounts, and web services for policy-based enrollment from non-domain or disconnected clients. TPM key attestation can confirm that a private key is protected by hardware, and newer releases add support for the ML-DSA post-quantum signature algorithm. Integration with Active Directory means endpoint information is reused during enrollment, while Group Policy controls which users and computers may receive which certificate types. Typical uses named on the page are S/MIME, secure Wi-Fi, VPN, IPsec, EFS, smart card logon, SSL/TLS and digital signatures. The page lists several Windows Server versions as supported and does not discuss licensing or limits.

activity-protocol.title: Activity Protocol – Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, Microsoft Learn
activity-protocol.notes: Activity Protocol is a standardized communication protocol used across many Microsoft SDKs, services and clients, including Copilot, Copilot Studio, Teams and the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK. It defines the shape of an Activity and how messages, events and interactions travel from a channel to agent code, so no channel-specific logic is needed. An Activity is a structured JSON object carrying sender, recipient, conversation context, originating channel, type and payload, with properties such as type, text and attachments. Defined types include message, conversation update, event, invoke and typing, and not every client supports each of them. For every incoming activity the SDK creates a turn context that is discarded when the turn ends, and replies are sent through methods on it. Attachments arrive on message activities with download links that are often short-lived, so files should be copied into own storage. Citations travel in the entities property rather than as attachments. Capabilities vary by channel: Teams supports adaptive cards and invoke actions, while non-Microsoft channels may render cards differently or not at all.

agent-quarantine.title: Agent quarantine API – Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft Learn
agent-quarantine.notes: Agent quarantine is a security and compliance measure that lets administrators isolate Copilot Studio agents that break rules, for example through data loss prevention violations or missing compliance documentation. Such agents may be detected through audits, runtime protection or admin reports. Quarantine is controlled through the Power Platform API in the copilotstudio namespace. One operation reads the current status, returning whether the agent is quarantined and when it was last updated, and two further operations set or clear the quarantined state. A quarantined agent stays visible to its makers and users in Copilot Studio but cannot interact with users. The typical flow is to flag a non-compliant agent, quarantine it, investigate and fix the issue, and then lift the quarantine. Callers need a Power Platform tenant admin, Power Platform administrator or Dynamics 365 service administrator role, the environment and bot IDs, and a valid Microsoft Entra token. The page covers only the API, not a user interface, and notes that the older powervirtualagents namespace is deprecated.

agent-runs.title: Threads, runs and messages – Foundry Agent Service (classic), Microsoft Learn
agent-runs.notes: A run is one invocation of an agent on a thread. The agent reads the thread's messages, uses its configuration, calls models and tools to do the work, and can append new messages with its answer. A typical flow starts a run, monitors its status until it finishes, and then retrieves the response. Run states are queued, in progress, requires action (when function-calling results are needed), completed, failed, cancelled and expired. An agent and a thread must exist beforehand, and in the standard setup threads are stored in an Azure Cosmos DB account. Conversational apps usually start a run after each user message. The page advises checking for failures, retrying with exponential backoff and polling the status at short intervals that grow for long operations. A thread can hold a very large number of messages, but long threads may add latency, so conversations should stay concise. The page does not give timeout values for expiry and states that classic agents are being retired in favor of the newer Foundry Agent Service.

agent-sponsor.title: Agent owners, sponsors and managers – Microsoft Entra Agent ID, Microsoft Learn
agent-sponsor.notes: An agent sponsor is a business representative who is accountable for an agent's purpose and lifecycle decisions but has no technical administrative access. Sponsors can be users, including guests, and certain group types. They decide on renewal or removal according to business need, justify access requests and, during security incidents, judge whether behavior is expected and approve actions such as suspension. Their permissions include requesting access packages for the agent, disabling agent identities, changing sponsors and soft-deleting, while changing application settings, authentication properties, restoring or hard-deleting are reserved for owners. Every agent identity and agent identity blueprint requires at least one sponsor, with a defined upper limit on sponsors and on groups among them. When an agent is created interactively, the calling user becomes sponsor automatically unless others are specified. Dynamic membership groups and assigned Microsoft 365 groups are allowed, while role-assignable groups and assigned security groups are not. The page suggests business owners, product managers or team leads as sponsors and recommends updating sponsorship when people change roles. It names no license requirements.

ai-form-fill-assistance.title: Form fill assistance – Power Apps, Microsoft Learn
ai-form-fill-assistance.notes: AI form fill assistance proposes values for form fields so data entry goes faster. Suggestions are optional and are saved only after the user reviews and accepts them, either one by one or all at once, and the source of each suggestion can be inspected. Suggestions draw on app usage, data already in the form and commonly used values. Smart Paste, offered as a preview, analyzes text or an image from the clipboard, and a files option reads uploaded documents of several text, PDF and image types, though files with sensitivity labels are not supported. The feature works in apps with the modern look, requires the environment feature and the column property for form fill assistance, and needs a Power Apps Premium license for model-driven apps or a Dynamics 365 Enterprise or Premium license for Dynamics apps. It applies to main and quick create forms and supports text, numeric, choice and date fields, but not columns protected by column security. Administrators can control it in the Power Platform admin center, and usage may be subject to service limits or throttling.

api-management-policies.title: Policies in Azure API Management – Microsoft Learn
api-management-policies.notes: Policies let API publishers change the behavior of an API in Azure API Management through configuration instead of code. A policy is a set of statements that run in sequence on a request or response at the gateway, between the API consumer and the managed API. Common uses are authentication, rate limiting, caching and transforming requests or responses, such as converting XML to JSON. Policies are written in XML with inbound, backend, outbound and on-error sections that run in that order, and they can be edited in a form-based or a code editor in the portal. Policy expressions use C# syntax with access to a context variable and a limited set of .NET types. Policies can be applied at global, workspace, product, API or operation scope, and the base element controls inheritance and evaluation order. When an error occurs, execution jumps to the on-error section. Policies are available in all service tiers. Not every policy works in every scope or section, and the page clearly separates them from Azure Policy, which is a governance service.

application-gateway-network-isolation.title: Private Application Gateway deployment – Microsoft Learn
application-gateway-network-isolation.notes: Network isolation for Azure Application Gateway allows v2 gateways to be deployed with a private-only frontend IP and no public IP resource. The aim is to remove earlier restrictions on network security groups and route tables and to reduce the risk of data exfiltration. Previously a public frontend IP was needed so the GatewayManager service could reach the gateway. With the feature, inbound GatewayManager traffic no longer needs to be allowed, a deny-all outbound rule can be used, and the default route can be overridden, for example to send traffic through a network virtual appliance. Frontend and outbound options can be combined independently. Prerequisites include a v2 SKU, opt-in through feature registration that can take time to apply, and a subnet delegated to the application gateway resource provider. Limitations include no direct outbound internet access with a private-only frontend, no Private Link support, dropped traffic to some private endpoints over global peering, and conflicts when a BGP-learned default route forces tunneling. Deny-all rules can accidentally block health probes or client traffic.

attack-surface-reduction-rules.title: Attack surface reduction rules overview – Microsoft Learn
attack-surface-reduction-rules.notes: Attack surface reduction rules are a Microsoft Defender Antivirus feature on Windows that target risky software behavior often abused by malware. Examples include launching scripts that download or run files, running obfuscated scripts, spawning child processes from Office apps and injecting code into other processes. Because legitimate software can behave similarly, the page urges testing. The rules are split into a small group of standard protection rules, which Microsoft recommends enabling in block mode, and further rules that should first run in audit mode. Available modes are off, block, audit, not configured and warn, and audit events show up in Windows event logs and advanced hunting. The feature needs Defender Antivirus as the active primary antivirus with real-time and cloud protection enabled, and it is not available on Linux or macOS. It applies to Defender for Endpoint Plan 1 and Plan 2 and does not strictly require Microsoft 365 E5, although E5 adds monitoring and reporting in the Defender portal. Rules can be deployed with Intune, Group Policy, Configuration Manager, PowerShell or other MDM tools. Exclusions weaken protection, since excluded files run without any events being recorded.

authorization-code-flow.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow – Microsoft identity platform, Microsoft Learn
authorization-code-flow.notes: The OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant lets a client application obtain access to protected resources such as web APIs on behalf of a signed-in user. It is based on the OAuth 2.0 specification and needs a user agent that can handle redirects, such as a browser, desktop or mobile app. The app first sends an authorization request, receives a short-lived code, and then redeems it at the token endpoint for an access token, optionally with a refresh token when offline access is requested and an ID token when OpenID Connect scopes are used. PKCE is recommended for all application types and required for single-page apps. Confidential clients authenticate with a secret or certificate, while public clients such as native apps and SPAs must not use secrets when redeeming the code. The app must be registered in Microsoft Entra with a client ID, and the redirect URI must match a registered value exactly. Admin-restricted scopes need administrator consent. Refresh tokens for SPAs expire after a fixed period, which then requires a new interactive sign-in. Microsoft recommends using an authentication library such as MSAL instead of raw HTTP requests.

auto-labeling.title: Apply a sensitivity label to content automatically – Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Learn
auto-labeling.notes: Auto-labeling assigns a sensitivity label to files and emails automatically when content matches configured conditions, or recommends a label to the user. This removes the need to train users on classification rules or rely on them labeling correctly. There are two methods. The client-side method runs in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook as people work and leaves the accept-or-decline decision to the user. The service-side method uses auto-labeling policies for content stored in SharePoint and OneDrive and for emails handled by Exchange Online, works regardless of app version and supports simulation before enforcement, but does not offer recommendations. Conditions can use sensitive information types, trainable classifiers, file properties and, for email, sender, recipient and header patterns. Manually applied labels are not overwritten by default. The page lists Microsoft 365 E5 or equivalent compliance licensing as a prerequisite, and E3 and Business Premium are not included. Limits apply to daily labeled files, number of policies and selected locations. Open or checked-out files are not labeled, and visual markings are not applied by policies.

avd-host-pool.title: Azure Virtual Desktop terminology – Microsoft Learn
avd-host-pool.notes: A host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop is a collection of Azure virtual machines registered as session hosts, and the VMs should be created from the same image for a consistent experience. Resources are published to users through application groups. Host pools are either personal or pooled. In a personal pool each user is assigned a session host and only one session runs per host, which gives dedicated desktops. In a pooled pool sessions are distributed across hosts using breadth-first or depth-first load balancing up to a configurable session limit, which lowers cost through sharing, and FSLogix is recommended for user data. Autoscale behaves differently per type, and updates come from Windows Update or other tools for personal hosts and from redeploying updated images for pooled hosts. Session hosts can be managed with the session host configuration approach, where the service handles the lifecycle, or with the standard approach, where the customer does it manually. A host pool can also serve as a validation environment for service updates. Desktop application groups work with both types, while RemoteApp groups work only with pooled pools.

azure-ai-document-intelligence.title: What is Azure AI Document Intelligence – Microsoft Learn
azure-ai-document-intelligence.notes: Azure AI Document Intelligence is a cloud service that applies machine learning based OCR and document processing to pull data out of forms and documents. It is positioned for structured documents and uses deterministic extraction, while complex, unstructured or multimodal content points to LLM-based analyzers in Content Understanding. Document analysis models such as Read and Layout extract printed and handwritten text, tables and structure. Prebuilt models cover invoices, receipts, contracts, bank statements, identity documents, business cards and several tax and mortgage forms. Custom models are trained on labeled data and come as neural, template and composed variants, and a custom classifier can identify document types before extraction. Extracted values are returned with types such as string, date, currency or address. Add-on capabilities include high-resolution OCR, formulas, fonts, barcodes, searchable PDFs, query fields and key-value pairs, and some premium add-ons carry extra cost. Developers can use Document Intelligence Studio, a REST API or SDKs for several languages. Typical uses are accounts payable, expense handling, compliance, KYC and tax or loan documentation, and older API versions are scheduled for retirement.

azure-automation-state-configuration.title: Azure Automation State Configuration overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-automation-state-configuration.notes: Azure Automation State Configuration is a configuration management service for writing, managing and compiling PowerShell Desired State Configuration configurations. It works for nodes in any cloud or on premises, imports DSC resources and assigns configurations to target nodes. A built-in pull server lets nodes fetch their configuration, move toward the desired state and report their status, so no separate pull server is needed. The portal shows how compliant each machine is, and report data can be forwarded to a Log Analytics workspace. Supported machines include Azure VMs, Windows and Linux machines on premises or in other clouds, with specific Windows Server and client versions listed. Azure nodes receive the required management framework or DSC for Linux automatically, and proxy support depends on the operating system version. Managing Azure VMs has no extra charge when the DSC extension meets a minimum version. The page announces that the service will be retired and recommends moving to Azure Machine Configuration, which also covers hybrid machines through Azure Arc. Continuous deployment pipelines are named as a typical scenario.

azure-backup-soft-delete.title: Soft delete for Azure Backup – Microsoft Learn
azure-backup-soft-delete.notes: Soft delete for Azure Backup delays the permanent removal of backup data, and in preview also of vaults, so deleted items stay recoverable for a retention period. It is meant to help after accidental or malicious deletion, such as ransomware or attacker activity, and it also helps with threats discovered late. The protection is on by default, cannot be switched off in regions where it is enforced, and is always on for new vaults. The default retention period is configurable within a stated range. Restored items return in a stop-protection-with-retain-data state, from which further restores or resumed protection are possible. A vault that still contains soft-deleted items is itself soft-deleted when removed through the portal and can be recovered within the period. Recovery points dropped through policy changes also remain soft-deleted. The shorter retention is free for vault backups, while longer periods incur regular backup charges. Soft delete does not cover some items, such as log recovery points for SQL Server and SAP HANA. After retention ends the data is deleted permanently, and old client versions may delete items immediately.

azure-database-for-postgresql-flexible-s.title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL documentation – Microsoft Learn
azure-database-for-postgresql-flexible-s.notes: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server is a fully managed database-as-a-service built on the open-source PostgreSQL engine and run on Azure. The documentation landing page presents it as suitable for mission-critical workloads that need predictable performance, security, high availability and scalability, and as a base for AI applications through native vector embedding support. Topics grouped on the page include high availability, geo-restore to the paired region, backup and restore, compute and storage scaling, read replicas and elastic clusters for horizontal scale. Security and networking content covers private endpoints, Microsoft Entra authentication and data encryption. For AI scenarios the page links to pgvector, DiskANN, Apache AGE for graph data and integrations with Semantic Kernel, LangChain, LlamaIndex and GraphRAG. Data can be mirrored into Microsoft Fabric. Tooling includes Azure CLI, Bicep, Terraform, a Python SDK, a Visual Studio Code extension and a REST API. A migration service supports offline and online moves from several sources, including Amazon RDS, Aurora and Google Cloud SQL. The page itself lists no limits or license terms.

azure-developer-cli.title: Azure Developer CLI reference – Microsoft Learn
azure-developer-cli.notes: The Azure Developer CLI, or azd, is meant to simplify the end-to-end developer workflow on Azure. It offers high-level commands for initializing a project, provisioning infrastructure, deploying code and monitoring, usable from a terminal, an IDE or CI/CD pipelines. Compared with Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell, it has fewer but broader commands, while those tools give fine-grained control over single resources. Projects are based on templates, most of which contain folders for environment configuration, infrastructure files in Bicep or Terraform and application source code, plus an azure.yaml file that maps services to Azure resources. Core commands include init for starting from a template, provision for creating resources, package and deploy for application code, and up, which runs provisioning, packaging and deployment in one step. Further commands monitor the app, configure a pipeline, manage environments such as development or production, and remove created resources with down. The compose command is in alpha status. The page lists no prerequisites, costs or license details.

azure-device-registry.title: Azure Device Registry overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-device-registry.notes: Azure Device Registry is a unified registry that represents IoT devices and assets as Azure Resource Manager resources, each with its own resource ID. It serves as the shared Azure control plane for Azure IoT Operations and Azure IoT Hub. Because devices and assets are ordinary Azure resources, teams can govern them with role-based access control, tags, resource groups and Azure Policy, and query them across departments with Azure Resource Graph. Namespaces form the management and security boundary, and every device and asset belongs to exactly one namespace. Schema registries store message definitions used by data flows for edge asset messages. Certificate management can issue, renew and revoke X.509 certificates for IoT Hub devices through a Microsoft-managed or customer-owned certificate authority. Groups, jobs and software updates are available as previews for IoT Hub, and for production updates the page points to Device Update for IoT Hub. Management actions let users call operations on southbound assets. Availability differs by service and region, and several capabilities carry preview status.

azure-dns-alias-record.title: Azure DNS alias records overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-dns-alias-record.notes: An Azure DNS alias record is a qualification on a DNS record set that makes it point to another Azure resource instead of a fixed value. The record set follows the target dynamically, so it updates itself at resolution time when, for instance, the IP address of a public IP resource changes. This avoids dangling DNS records that point to resources that no longer exist, and it allows a record at the zone apex, where CNAME records are not permitted. Alias records are supported for A, AAAA and CNAME record types. Possible targets include a standard-SKU public IP, a Traffic Manager profile, an Azure CDN endpoint, an Azure Front Door endpoint and another record set in the same zone. Typical uses are load balancing at the apex through Traffic Manager, pointing a bare domain at a CDN endpoint for a static website, and branding custom domains for Front Door. The Microsoft.Network resource provider must be registered. A limit of alias record sets per resource applies, apex references to Akamai-based CDN endpoints are unsupported, and new Traffic Manager setups are encouraged to use linked records.

azure-functions-consumption-plan.title: Azure Functions Consumption plan hosting – Microsoft Learn
azure-functions-consumption-plan.notes: The Consumption plan is a serverless hosting option for Azure Functions, and the page now labels it as legacy, recommending the Flex Consumption plan for new function apps. The Functions host adds and removes instances dynamically depending on the number of incoming events, so apps scale automatically even under heavy load. Billing covers compute only while functions run and is based on the number of executions, execution time and memory used, aggregated across all functions in an app. Each execution times out after a configurable period. Several apps in the same region can share one plan and still scale independently, although a separate plan per app is suggested and a maximum number of apps per plan exists. The page states that this plan is currently the only serverless option that supports Windows. Linux in the Consumption plan has a scheduled retirement date, gets no new features or language versions, and apps on an end-of-life runtime will stop running. Flex Consumption is offered only on Linux, so Windows apps must change operating system when migrating.

azure-functions-triggers-and-bindings.title: Azure Functions triggers and bindings concepts – Microsoft Learn
azure-functions-triggers-and-bindings.notes: In Azure Functions, a trigger defines how a function is invoked, and every function has exactly one trigger, which can also pass data into the function. A binding is a declarative connection to another resource: an input binding delivers data to the function, and an output binding sends data out, while a trigger is a special kind of input binding. Bindings spare developers from hard-coding access to other services, since data arrives through parameters and leaves through the return value. A function may have no, one or several bindings. They are defined differently per language, for example through attributes, annotations, function.json, decorators or objects in the Node.js library. Supported services include Blob Storage, Cosmos DB, Event Grid, Event Hubs, HTTP, Service Bus, Queue Storage and Timer, among others. All bindings except HTTP and timer require registering a binding extension. Kafka and RabbitMQ triggers are not supported in the Consumption plan. Bindings are optional, because code can use an Azure SDK client instead, and names may contain only letters, digits and underscores. Custom bindings must be written in .NET.

azure-horizondb.title: Azure HorizonDB overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-horizondb.notes: Azure HorizonDB is a cloud-native, fully managed database service based on PostgreSQL, currently in preview. It separates compute from storage and follows a database-as-a-log design. A cluster consists of one or more compute replicas, with exactly one writable primary and the rest readable standbys, all sharing a single copy of data in zone-redundant storage. A read-write endpoint always targets the primary, and a read-only endpoint distributes connections across readable replicas. Zonal resilience needs at least two replicas. Tasks such as write-ahead log shipping and archiving, checkpoints, backups and recovery are handled by the storage layer, which grows automatically without configuring size or IOPS. Billing is based on provisioned core hours, database storage and backup storage. Intended uses include transactional workloads, AI applications with vector search, read scale-out and mirroring to Fabric OneLake. The page lists current gaps, such as configurable backup retention, cross-region read replicas, customer-managed keys, configurable maintenance windows, built-in connection pooling and virtual network injection, and the service is offered only in selected regions.

azure-nd-gb200-v6.title: ND GB200 v6 size series – Microsoft Learn
azure-nd-gb200-v6.notes: The ND GB200 v6 series is a family of GPU-accelerated Azure virtual machines built on NVIDIA GB200 Tensor Core GPUs with the Blackwell architecture. The series has a single size, with Grace CPUs, four Blackwell GPUs and a large pool of memory per VM, local NVMe storage and Ethernet networking. NVLink connects GPUs within a VM, and NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand provides scale-out connectivity that is tuned for NCCL-based tools. At system level the VMs are grouped into NVL72 racks that contain 72 GPUs, built from groups of ND GB200 v6 VMs. The page names deep learning training, generative AI and HPC as the target workloads and mentions out-of-the-box support for TensorFlow, PyTorch, JAX and RAPIDS. Generation 2 VMs are supported and generation 1 is not, and a vCPU quota is needed. Premium storage, premium storage caching, accelerated networking and ephemeral OS disks are supported. Live migration, memory-preserving updates, nested virtualization and service healing are not supported. The page gives no license or pricing details.
